title: Asana
description: Move beyond the physical and understand Asana as a meditative state of being—steady, comfortable, and perfectly balanced.

sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas
sections.gurudevInsight: The husk is gone, the sprout moves though it & comes up. They are (1) Yama (2) Niyama (3) Aasana (4) Pranayama (5) Pratyahara (6) Dhyana (7) Dharana (8) Samadhi. He goes into the details of each & what is the result that you can expect from each one of them. Yoga has 8 limbs, like a chair has got four legs, yoga has 8 limbs, or legs. So you just pull one, everything else will come down. If you pull one leg of the chair whole chair comes.

sutra.meaning: The posture should be steady and comfortable.

sections.gurudevInsight: Aasana: - Sthiramsukhamasana - That which is steady & which is comfortable is the asana. Normally, when we are comfortable, we are not steady, we are not sitting erect but when we are erect, we are so stiff, we are not comfortable. But asana is when you are both steady & comfortable, you are erect, steady & at the same time comfortable.

sutra.meaning: It results in relaxation of effort and the meeting with the infinite.

sections.insight: Yogic practices should feel pleasureable to be sustained.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Am I making my life more satvic and the body more healthy?
sections.journalPrompt: Did I feel relaxed after yoga.
sections.gurudevInsight:
Prayatnashaitalya anant samapattibhaam - Letting go the effort, main point of it & feeling the body, letting go the effort & experiencing the infinity. Have you noticed, after you do asanas, how it feels? Sit in a comfortable posture happily - sukhsmasana –
pleasurable. Feel as though it’s a pleasure just to be, just to sit, that is sukha. How do you
approach pleasure? Oh great wonderful. Have you ever sat steadily & wonderful just to be,
just to sit? So do once & you will see how it feels. Prayatnashaitalya – letting go of all the
efforts & feeling the infinity & what is the effect of it? What does it do?

sutra.meaning: From then on, there are no botherations from the dualities like happiness and distress, heat and cold.

Tatodhwandana
vidhata - It hits the duality or the conflicts in you. It roots out the conflicts in you. Any time
you are confused, your mind is in conflict, do asana, you will see right away clarity comes.
Effect of asana is clearing all conflicts, duality.

sutra.meaning: Once this is accomplished, regulation of the incoming and the outgoing breath with retention is attained.

sections.insight: Prana is the all permeating, auto generated  energy which sustains and destroys life. It is also at the heart of the practice of yoga.  Pranayama consists of prana + ayama ie regulation. Prana is vital to maintaining life and the systems of the body. Pranayama helps to keep its free flow.

sections.shlokaFrom: अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे |प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणा: || 29|| अपरे नियताहारा: प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति |सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषा: || 30||
sections.wisdomFrom: Still others offer as sacrifice the outgoing breath in the incoming breath, while some offer the incoming breath into the outgoing breath. Some arduously practice prāṇāyām and restrain the incoming and outgoing breaths, purely absorbed in the regulation of the life-energy. Yet others curtail their food intake and offer the breath into the life-energy as sacrifice. All these knowers of sacrifice are cleansed of their impurities as a result of such performances.
sections.gurudevInsight:
In
that state of Asana, unique state of asana, obstructing the flow of breath that is natural. Here
he says, obstructing the natural flow because your flow is not natural at all. We have made
our breath so unnatural by being unnatural, so what ever now is natural is not natural. We
have to revert back, so how do we revert back? Not just accepting what is, however the
breath is going on, I accept it - no. Break its movements; break the movement of breath by
consciously breathing deep, long, subtle with counts & having attention at different places.
